RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not itself evidence of bias. In fields like municipal planning, senior panels are often male simply because of who holds the senior posts. On its own it proves nothing, and leading with it can make a strong complaint look weak.

Your stronger facts are the credential gap — a master's, a licence and twelve years against a bachelor's and unquantified "consultation experience" — and the unanswered request for written reasons.

So: pursue the reasons, in writing, citing any policy or statutory deadline. Ask what criteria were weighted and how each candidate scored. Mention panel composition only as context if the reasons turn out to be thin or evasive.
